newsitem.title: USA: Voters in 17 Illinois counties approve tax limits.
newsitem.headline: Voters in 17 Illinois counties approve tax limits.

text.p: Voters in 17 Illinois counties approved limits on local property tax increases in Tuesday's election, county clerk offices reported Wednesday.
The 17 counties that approved tax caps were Macoupin, Schuyler, Champaign, Kankakee, Boone, Christian, Franklin, Jackson, Lee, Logan, Monroe, Morgan, Menard, Randolph, Sangamon Union and Winnebago.

According to the Illinois Board of Elections, 19 Illinois counties had opted to place the tax cap referendum on Tuesday's ballot in accordance with a new law that allowed 96 county boards outside of the Chicago area to decide whether to hold a vote on tax limitations.
Only Massac and Williamson county voters turned down the tax limits, county clerks reported.
Tax caps are already in place in six Chicago area counties where they limit annual increases in local property tax collections to five percent or the rate of inflation, whichever is less.
The restriction also prohibits the issuance of general obligation debt without voter approval.
